ownRead.statement:
**Date:** 2026-09-30  
**Target:** existing RRG v0.2 locked core.  
**Core-definition changes:** none.  
**Purpose:** record additional mathematical results and experiments against existing claims, not propose a replacement theory.

## Source and claim conventions

Section numbers below refer to `00_LOCKED_CORE.md`: §3 geometry–mode reciprocity; §4 RRG closure during an interval; §5 heterogeneous higher-level formation with internal dynamics retained; §6 variation; §7 scale-dependent effective units/mechanisms; §8 structural recursion; §9 optional formation/propagation mechanisms.

“Supports core” means that the reported system realizes the specified relationship. It does not claim that the authors tested RRG by name, nor that one successful example proves every possible application. Model assumptions and experimental conditions belong to the cited realization, not to the locked definitions.

## Additional evidence


### E01 — He et al. (2019)

**Formation of optical supramolecular structures in a fibre laser by tailoring long-range soliton interactions**  
Nature Communications 10, 5756. DOI: [10.1038/s41467-019-13746-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-13746-6)

**Classification:** supports core / domain-specific realization.  
**Evidence:** Experiment with theoretical modelling.  
**Existing clauses:** §3, §5, §6, §7, §8.

Mixed assemblies contain single pulses, pairs and triplets; internal pair dynamics coexist with larger-scale optical–acoustic organization.

**Scope:** Designed, pumped fibre-laser system; optical molecules are bound pulses, not chemical molecules.

**Checked:** Full primary paper and supplementary text; Figure 3 inspected as a rendered page.  
**Location:** Main paper: Results, Elementary diversity; Figures 1 and 3; Supplementary Note 8.  
**Inspected source:** https://photonics.umbc.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/688/2022/02/PAJ296.pdf


### E02 — Weng et al. (2020)

**Heteronuclear soliton molecules in optical microresonators**  
Nature Communications. DOI: [10.1038/s41467-020-15720-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-15720-z)

**Classification:** supports core / domain-specific realization.  
**Evidence:** Experiment with theoretical modelling.  
**Existing clauses:** §3, §5, §6.

Pulses with distinct carrier frequencies and amplitudes bind while their relative phase continues evolving.

**Scope:** Driven Kerr microresonator; distinguish carrier frequency from collective repetition rate.

**Checked:** Full primary author manuscript, cross-checked against publisher record.  
**Location:** Introduction; Figures 1–4; electro-optic measurements and coupled Lugiato–Lefever modelling.  
**Inspected source:** https://arxiv.org/html/1901.04026v5


### E03 — Fu et al. (2023)

**Mechanochemical feedback loop drives persistent motion of liposomes**  
Nature Physics 19, 1211–1218. DOI: [10.1038/s41567-023-02058-8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41567-023-02058-8)

**Classification:** supports core / domain-specific realization.  
**Evidence:** Experiment plus reduced mechanochemical model.  
**Existing clauses:** §3, §4, §5.

Protein distributions deform vesicles; deformation and motion reorganize the proteins, sustaining a reciprocal loop.

**Scope:** Reconstituted lipid/protein system with ATP; the simulation uses a phenomenological movement coupling.

**Checked:** Full primary article, methods and figure descriptions.  
**Location:** Figures 1–4; Extended Data Figures 6–8; Results on geometry-sensitive protein redistribution.  
**Inspected source:** https://www.nature.com/articles/s41567-023-02058-8


### E04 — Godino et al. (2019)

**De novo synthesized Min proteins drive oscillatory liposome deformation and regulate FtsA–FtsZ cytoskeletal patterns**  
Nature Communications 10, 4969. DOI: [10.1038/s41467-019-12932-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-12932-w)

**Classification:** supports core / domain-specific realization.  
**Evidence:** Experiment.  
**Existing clauses:** §3, §5, §6.

Proteins synthesized from DNA templates develop collective dynamics accompanied by liposome deformation and cytoskeletal reorganization.

**Scope:** Synthetic cellular compartment; not the creation of a complete self-reproducing organism.

**Checked:** Full primary article and figure descriptions.  
**Location:** Abstract and Results on cell-free Min expression, membrane deformation and FtsA–FtsZ organization.  
**Inspected source:** https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-019-12932-w


### E05 — Prindle et al. (2015)

**Ion channels enable electrical communication in bacterial communities**  
Nature 527, 59–63. DOI: [10.1038/nature15709](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature15709)

**Classification:** supports core / domain-specific realization.  
**Evidence:** Experiment with interventions.  
**Existing clauses:** §3, §5, §7.

Potassium-mediated signals coordinate biofilm metabolic activity; potassium clamping suppresses the measured membrane-potential oscillations.

**Scope:** Bacillus subtilis biofilms under the reported growth conditions.

**Checked:** Primary publisher text and extended-data figure descriptions.  
**Location:** Electrical signalling mechanism; Extended Data Figure 3, potassium-clamp intervention.  
**Inspected source:** https://www.nature.com/articles/nature15709


### E06 — Liu et al. (2017)

**Coupling between distant biofilms and emergence of nutrient time-sharing**  
Science 356, 638–642. DOI: [10.1126/science.aah4204](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aah4204)

**Classification:** supports core / domain-specific realization.  
**Evidence:** Experiment testing a coupled-oscillator prediction.  
**Existing clauses:** §5, §7, §8.

Two biofilms coordinate oscillations; nutrient conditions induce predicted in-phase or antiphase relationships.

**Scope:** A coupled community pair, not physical fusion into one organism.

**Checked:** Primary abstract and detailed figure captions reproduced in PubMed; full manuscript was not accessible.  
**Location:** Abstract; Figures 1–3, especially phase diagrams and experimental validations in Figure 2.  
**Inspected source:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28386026/


### E07 — Tikhomirov, Petersen and Qian (2017)

**Fractal assembly of micrometre-scale DNA origami arrays with arbitrary patterns**  
Nature 552, 67–71. DOI: [10.1038/nature24655](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature24655)

**Classification:** supports core / domain-specific realization.  
**Evidence:** Engineered molecular self-assembly experiment.  
**Existing clauses:** §5, §6, §7, §8, §9.

Designed DNA tiles assemble through successive stages into larger arrays used in further assembly.

**Scope:** Direct structural-recursion evidence; not a measurement of a full multiscale temporal spectrum.

**Checked:** Primary abstract and accessible publisher figure descriptions; subscription full text not inspected.  
**Location:** Abstract and hierarchical assembly scheme.  
**Inspected source:** https://www.nature.com/articles/nature24655


### E08 — Baumann et al. (2010)

**Dicke quantum phase transition with a superfluid gas in an optical cavity**  
Nature 464, 1301–1306. DOI: [10.1038/nature09009](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature09009)

**Classification:** supports core / domain-specific realization.  
**Evidence:** Quantum-gas experiment with quantitative threshold comparison.  
**Existing clauses:** §3, §4, §5, §6.

Atomic density organization and the cavity field reinforce one another; measured phase boundaries agree with the specified mean-field model.

**Scope:** Pumped atom–cavity system; its threshold equation is domain-specific.

**Checked:** Full primary author manuscript; publisher record and figure descriptions cross-checked.  
**Location:** Self-organization mechanism; Figure 5 and Methods equations 6–9.  
**Inspected source:** https://arxiv.org/html/0912.3261v1


### E09 — Pecora et al. (2014)

**Cluster synchronization and isolated desynchronization in complex networks with symmetries**  
Nature Communications 5, 4079. DOI: [10.1038/ncomms5079](https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms5079)

**Classification:** supports core / domain-specific realization.  
**Evidence:** Mathematical derivation plus electro-optic experiment.  
**Existing clauses:** §3, §5, §7.

Network symmetries predict collective clusters and their dynamical changes; experiments test those predictions.

**Scope:** Specified oscillator/network assumptions; they are not added as requirements of RRG.

**Checked:** Full primary author manuscript; publisher metadata cross-checked. Manuscript title differs slightly.  
**Location:** Equations 1–2; group-orbit construction; Figure 3 and block-decomposed variational equations.  
**Inspected source:** https://arxiv.org/html/1309.6605v1


## What the added evidence supports

The entries map to complementary parts of the locked core rather than impose an identical microscopic mechanism:

| Existing claim | Additional entries |
|---|---|
| Reciprocal influence of organization and active modes | E01, E03, E08 |
| Different constituents/internal modes can participate in one collective organization | E01, E02, E04 |
| Lower organization can remain inside a larger arrangement | E01, E02 |
| Organized groups can enter a further collective relationship | E01, E05 + E06 |
| Successive assembly stages can use previous structures as units | E07 |
| Organization can make quantitative predictions about collective dynamics | E06, E08, E09 |

These are experiments and restricted mathematical results. They strengthen the evidence for the specified RRG relationships. They do not derive the four forces or prove a universal cosmological mechanism; those remain the separately labelled extensions in the unchanged core.

## Research changes versus definition changes

No new stability threshold, mandatory duplication step, identical-component requirement, or universal-equation requirement is introduced here. No numerical simulation was run for this addendum. All experimental results are those of the cited authors.

ownRead.plainLanguage:
This register reports experiments and restricted mathematical results against existing core clauses. “Supports core” is the register’s classification; it does not mean the cited authors tested RRG by name or proved every application.

“Checked”, “Location” and “Inspected source” describe checks reported by the supplied document, not new paper inspections by this website. In particular, E06 reports abstract/figure access without a full manuscript, and E07 reports abstract/figure access without subscription full text. All experimental results belong to the cited authors. No numerical simulation was run for the addendum.

The register’s E01–E09 correspond to the stable website IDs :claim[UT-E01], :claim[UT-E02], :claim[UT-E03], :claim[UT-E04], :claim[UT-E05], :claim[UT-E06], :claim[UT-E07], :claim[UT-E08] and :claim[UT-E09].
